source: Feature-regression prevention rules (adopted 2026-10-11). They complement the review-pass product-preservation preflight, which applies to all feature work including non-governed projects; these rules never replace or weaken it, and its surface set, authority, and evidence requirements apply in full.
when_to_read: Before writing a plan, design, or work instruction or requesting a review, before a completion report, and when starting to recover from drift (work that departed from what the requester asked for).

terms.requester quote: A sentence the requester (a human) wrote in an issue, chat, or meeting note, quoted verbatim with its date and source. An AI summary, inference, or 'effectively decided' is not a quote.
terms.baseline: The last commit where the affected feature worked correctly, before the regression.
terms.user entry point: Any surface through which a user or a dependent system reaches a feature: UI route or navigation, screen, button, URL, API, CLI command, library export, data schema, job, package or deployment target, and operations or handoff path (the review-pass preflight surface examples; a kind that does not apply needs an explicit N/A reason).

rules.remove_needs_requester_quote: Write an instruction that removes or disables a user-visible feature (screen, button, path, free feature) only with a dated requester quote that asks for it. AI inference or coordinator judgment is not grounds for removal; without the quote the review fails.
rules.coordinator_decision_not_basis: A decision without a requester quote, or marked unconfirmed, withdrawn, or superseded, is not a basis. Do not turn an implementation into a decision ('it is already on dev, so it is decided').
rules.keep_baseline_section: An instruction or plan that touches existing behavior has a 'Existing behavior to keep' section: the baseline commit and, one per line, each user entry point that passes through the changed code path, marked 'applies' with how it will be checked or 'does not apply' with a reason.
rules.impossible_needs_evidence: Claim 'technically impossible' or 'not supported' only together with the search result that found the previously working implementation (file:line) and a run result. Without them the review fails.
rules.deletion_needs_basis: When a code change deletes user feature files or tests, the change description has a 'Deletion basis' section giving, per file, a requester quote or the number of an issue that contains the requester's request for it (an issue number without such a quote is not a basis). A deleted test is replaced by one that exercises real behavior; a mock-only test is never the sole evidence.
rules.done_needs_all_entrypoints: Report pass or completion only with evidence that every user entry point on the changed path was actually checked the same way as on the baseline (browser check, smoke output, served URL). Never widen a partial flow or a single measurement into an overall pass.
rules.requester_quote_fail_not_overridden: When a review FAIL is grounded in a requester quote, the coordinator does not override it. Fix it and pass a re-review of the same target; escalate to the requester only when it cannot be fixed.
rules.repeat_review_triage: After 5 review FAILs on the same target (every 4 after a triage), get a triage verdict (continue, wrong instruction, or over-review) from a stronger model different from the implementer and reviewer, given the whole FAIL history, before the next round. Within one review stage, the same target path is the same target even under a different issue or gate; with a different path, it is the same target only when both the issue and the gate are the same. Changing the path together with the issue or the gate starts new work. Drop a finding only when the verdict is wrong instruction or over-review, the issue records the path of that round's stored result copy and quotes from that copy, verbatim, both the finding and the verdict's reason, and that round has no FAIL grounded in a requester quote (if any finding of the round rests on a requester quote, nothing from that round is dropped). Findings grounded in a requester quote are never dropped.
rules.subtask_quotes_mission: Every subtask and review request carries a 'Goal:' line that quotes the requester's goal verbatim. Coordinator summaries go only in a separate 'Coordinator interpretation' field.
rules.drift_recovery_order: Recover from drift in this order: 1) pin the goal 2) map the contaminated scope 3) quarantine-delete the wrong code and documents 4) assess, analyze gaps, design, then build. Procedure: docs/guides/drift-recovery.md
